entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] If Taleghani Had Read Hobbes! The late Seyyed Mahmoud Taleghani, in the seven…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

If Taleghani Had Read Hobbes!
The late Seyyed Mahmoud Taleghani, in the seven months of his life after the 1979 Revolution, enjoyed a popularity beyond imagination. From his words, the general public sensed a suffering, a sincerity, and a purity in which no selfish personal, factional, or ideological motive had any part. Even those segments of the people who were disgruntled with the revolution and loyal to the monarchical system sincerely held him dear and regarded him as being of a different kind. In truth, the late Taleghani was indeed of a different kind. The resonance of his clear voice in the environment of the University of Tehran acted like the blowing of a pleasant and gentle breeze upon hearts fearful and anxious about the fire of the power-seeking conflicts of the age. His voice was full of a spiritual freshness yet accompanied by much sorrow, warning, and deep concern about the future. It was as if he knew what lay ahead. He knew well many of his peers and the various political organizations of that day, and he knew precisely what goal each of them was pursuing behind their pompous and hollow slogans. He did not enter into the game of any of them, nor did he consent to the elimination and exclusion of any of them. He tried to offer a rule for the coexistence of all of them within a pluralist framework, but it was as if he knew how the story would unfold! He concealed his suffering, sorrow, distress, dissatisfaction, and desperation, but it seemed that the poisonous draught of self-consumption and self-restraint wore down his frail and ailing body and took his life. It was as if, in despair of the notables, he sought hope in the masses of the people. He held an optimism and a pleasant feeling toward the common, nameless, and unheralded people. He regarded them as beings endowed with an innate nature (fitrat), and in his view human nature was fashioned from goodness and virtue. Perhaps for this reason, he considered the delegation of the decision-making system to the masses of the people in the form of various councils to be the only path to political salvation. In his view, consultation, deliberation, and the council were the foundation of prophetic politics. For this reason, he insisted firmly on the establishment of councils at all levels of political and social life. In considering the masses of the people as endowed with innate nature, perhaps his own inclinations were also involved. Or perhaps, in his definition of human nature, he had allowed one side of the human species' disposition to dominate the other side more than it should. Whatever it was, it seemed far too idealistic for Iranian society. Perhaps Mr. Taleghani needed to read Plato through the eyes of Strauss, or Hobbes's Leviathan.
In any case, he was a human being of unparalleled integrity and, in every respect, immaculate, pure, and great—one of those of whom there should be more in the human world, but there are not. May his lofty and long-suffering soul be in the presence of God's grace and mercy at the highest degree of existence. #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] On the Moscow train, the St. Petersburg to Moscow route was high-speed. Of…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

On the Moscow train, the St. Petersburg to Moscow route was high-speed. Of course, its speed never exceeded 199 kilometers per hour. It covered the roughly 800-kilometer distance between the two cities in exactly 4 hours. The route was entirely flat and forested, covered with young trees. Occasionally, a farm would appear in the middle of the forests. The train passed by several small towns and stopped for only one minute at just two or three intermediate stations. The lush green steppes on both sides of the railway reminded me of a scene from Andrei Tarkovsky's film Mirror—the scene where a beautiful, sorrowful woman sits on the trunk of a dry, fallen tree, waiting for her husband to return from the war front. In that scene, when the wind sweeps through the meadow, it seems as if a glimpse of paradise appears on earth. As it happened, the male voice that informed passengers of the status of intermediate stations sounded like Tarkovsky's voice. The man's voice resonated in my ears like the recitation of a poem, as delicate as the murmur of a gentle autumn rain. I said to myself, how could such a seemingly rough alphabet produce words so fluent, delicate, and sweet? Moscow's air temperature was a few degrees higher than St. Petersburg's, but fortunately, it remained at a mild and pleasant level. Upon exiting the old railway station, Stalin's architectural legacy became evident before our eyes. The massive government buildings, known as the Seven Sisters, dominated central Moscow. They were built by Stalin's order to give grandeur to Moscow. From the very first moment of arriving in the capital, the impatience of its residents compared to those of St. Petersburg was apparent! This impatience manifested itself in the ear-splitting honks of some nervous and hasty drivers in the midday traffic. Our hotel was a skyscraper in what seemed to me a protected spot on the northwestern outskirts of Moscow. The security arrangements inside the hotel were also unexpected. A burly Russian man on the verge of old age, whose cold demeanor and icy gaze were no less than Vladimir Putin's own, monitored the passage of guests and their luggage through the electronic gate in the hotel lobby. He seemed to me like a retired KGB officer! Such visible care and surveillance were clearly linked to the war in Ukraine. In St. Petersburg, apart from a sense of ambiguity and concern in the depths of people's eyes, no other trace or sign of the war was visible. In Moscow, however, the security measures at the hotel and on some of the city's peripheral highways cast a shadow over the capital, however faint, revealing the war's presence. Nevertheless, overall, no sense of war-weariness was visible in the daily lives of the citizens. #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] There is no room left for denial! The Khorasan newspaper, which usually…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

There is no room left for denial! The Khorasan newspaper, which usually supports the positions of Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, in response to Masoud Pezeshkian's explicit references to the problems afflicting society and the country, wrote: "A large part of society, upon hearing these problems—especially from someone responsible for solving them—will surely feel bad about the future. This is exactly the outcome the enemy pursues in its media."

In reality, the story is exactly the opposite! When the president honestly and sincerely raises the problems of society, not only does a large part of society not feel bad, but they actually feel a bit of relief knowing that senior officials are aware of the multitude of problems in their lives and are informed of the dimensions of the issues!

The multitude of problems are too evident and tangible for the people to be ignored or concealed. Therefore, when an official tries to ignore or downplay the issues, society concludes that these people are trapped and imprisoned in their own closed bubble, unaware of what is happening at the societal level, and thus they are out of touch with reality!

For this reason, people feel extremely bad and bitter, thinking to themselves: When these people don't even know what situation we are in and how much we suffer from all these calamities, how can we expect them to solve any problem?

In contrast, when someone in the position of president acknowledges the problems, people say to themselves, at least thank goodness they themselves know what is going on!

The truth is that the era of sweeping garbage under the rug is over. You can sweep a single piece of garbage under the rug to hide it from guests, but a large number of them cannot be hidden. Just as the stench of accumulated trash seeps out from under the rug and exposes the homeowner's concealment, so too does the volume of society's big and small problems.

Those who, for whatever purpose, deny the volume of society's problems or downplay them do not create hope in people but rather fuel their anger and dissatisfaction.

When someone denies an object right before our eyes, the only feeling we get is that they are taking us for a fool! Human beings become provoked and angered when they are assumed to be fools.

#Ahmad_Zeydabadi
@ahmadzeidabad

How painful and heartbreaking! These days, whenever I intend to write about any issue, I remember that what comes to my mind about that issue, I have written about it in previous years not once or twice but many times! Two years ago, when war engulfed Lebanon, in this same channel, in a note titled "Waiting for Godot?" I wrote: "The more I scrutinize the statements of the country's official authorities, in the face of a war that has fallen like fire upon Lebanon's harvest, I see no clear plan or strategy. Neither a clear plan for a ceasefire nor a vision for the continuation of the war. It is as if they are sitting waiting to see what happens! Their most important initiative is traveling to Beirut! These trips are not a bad thing from a propaganda standpoint, but which knot do they untie from the affairs of the afflicted people of Lebanon? Israel is practically emptying southern Lebanon of its Shia population and destroying the villages and towns of that region. This event completely disrupts Lebanon's demographic composition and, consequently, the type of political arrangement in that country. This is a danger whose consequences Gebran Bassil, the leader of the Christian party, the Free Patriotic Movement of Lebanon, has also warned about. Instead of empty slogans, officials should seek a way to end the war. Unfortunately, the hardline forces supporting the government have stripped the government of the courage for any diplomatic initiative and only beat the drum of war, without having any realistic assessment of its outcomes. The fate of such sitting on one's hands and waiting for Godot is clearer than to need a warning!" Oh God! How painful and heartbreaking it is that a person clearly sees the outcome of a policy on the horizon and warns of its occurrence with gentle language and reasoning, but those who should see or hear ignore it, and that event occurs in practice in its same ominous form!#احمد_زیدآبادی@ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] ISIS-style intimidation! Meysam Nili, who appears to be the brother-in-law of…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

ISIS-style intimidation! Meysam Nili, who appears to be the brother-in-law of the late Raisi's son-in-law, has practically issued an ultimatum to the heads of the executive and judicial branches, writing in a tone full of menace and intimidation: "The definitive punishment for moharebeh (those waging war against God) in the Quran is nothing more than a few things: hanging, beheading, cutting off the hands and feet of opponents, or exile and banishment from the land. The foul beasts and hyenas of the coup plotters and the paid lackeys of Trump and Netanyahu have no right to return to the Islamic country or to continue living in this sacred land. These actions are against national unity and security, and the resurrected people will certainly not tolerate them"! Apparently, he is referring to the return of Mohsen Namjoo to the country and the possibility of similar actions by a number of other compatriots who have emigrated. It seems that this individual, firstly, does not know that the aforementioned punishments pertain to highway robbers, who are referred to in the Quran as "mohareb" (those who wage war). Secondly, if such rigid, frozen, and fossilized literalism were to be adopted, he should also be demanding jizya (poll tax) from the People of the Book and the revival of slavery! This illogical and rigid-minded literalism is exactly, without any reduction or addition, the same method and interpretation of ISIS and takfiri organizations in the Islamic world, who beheaded their opponents in front of cameras and took women and girls of different faiths as slaves! It was not without reason that the late Ayatollah Khomeini saw the greatest danger and threat to society as coming from the fossilized individuals who, through their bigotry, have dragged the Islamic world into decline. In fact, any teenager or young person unfamiliar with authentic religious texts and their various interpretations, upon seeing this kind of ISIS-style rhetoric, becomes horrified and disgusted with religion itself. It is strange that such intimidating and terror-inducing rhetoric is being promoted and propagated by these individuals at a time when the country is embroiled in a costly and unprecedented war, and on the other hand, all the efforts of the attackers and their supporters are aimed at portraying the entire nature of the political system as exactly this kind of violence! Claiming self-appointed representation on behalf of the "resurrected people" to promote terror in the country also seems to have become a new political business for such individuals! When, where, and by whom was this representation delegated to these people, of which no one is aware? While takfirism and ISIS-style extremism are on the decline in other parts of the Islamic world, unfortunately in our country it seems to have gained new momentum among a certain group. If a clear, precise, and distinct line is not drawn without delay between the official policy of the country and the supporters of such ISIS-like interpretations, unprecedented catastrophes will occur in the country. #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] The erosion of war and the capacity to think... Once again, American military…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

The erosion of war and the capacity to think... Once again, American military drones, missiles, and bombs have rained down on the people of the country's southern cities. Alongside material damage, a number of our compatriots have been killed. A wedding ceremony in Kohestak turned into a mourning gathering. In response, Iranian forces also targeted American bases in the Middle East with missiles. Everyone is asking: how long will these clashes continue, and where will they end? The truth is that there is no clear answer to these two questions. The American side holds contradictory positions. On one hand, they emphasize continuing pressure until the collapse of our country's security and economy, and on the other hand, they claim the goal of the pressure is to force the leaders of the Islamic Republic back to the negotiating table! On the Iranian side, despite the constant insistence by responsible officials on the need for social unity and cohesion, no single voice is heard regarding the war. While the leaders of the branches of government declare their goal to be the revival of the agreement and forcing America to implement its provisions, many other voices from within the establishment insist on opposing the agreement, continuing and expanding the war, and the necessity of resorting to preemptive operations. As such, the atmosphere on both sides of the war is ambiguous and unclear. As long as this remains the case, the war will continue intermittently along its current erosive path. The main issue, however, is: to what point can the war of attrition in its current form continue? It is clear that capacities on both sides of the war are limited, and it is impossible to sustain the current conditions even for the next few months. Therefore, it is highly likely that a dramatic event will change the current course. What will be the nature of that event, and in what direction will it shape the fate of the conflict? The nature of an "event" is its chance and accidental occurrence, and it is not predictable. Any prediction in this regard is like shooting an arrow in the dark. Even if such an arrow hits its target, it is by chance and not a sign of the predictor's knowledge and skill! In our culture, these events are called fate and destiny (qaza va qadar), and now our fate is tied to fate and destiny. All we can do is pray that the outcome is good. #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] At 61! Today I turned 61; of course, according to what's written in my ID,…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

At 61! Today I turned 61; of course, according to what's written in my ID, otherwise, according to my sisters, I was born in "Kol Kar," meaning the cotton planting season, which falls in April, from late Farvardin to mid Ordibehesht. Honestly, when I look back, I'm quite astonished at my own situation. The factors that came together to bring me from "Qaleh-ye Zardu," where I fell onto the mud floor of a dark, smoky room, to this vague present point—it's been like walking on quicksand. Was everything that happened mere coincidence? One could call it coincidence, especially in this century where not just an individual's life path but the entire universe is considered random, the result of blind forces colliding! Nevertheless, I believe every person assumes some kind of plan or destiny in the course of their life's evolution. Even those who believe in the randomness of existence are tempted, when facing grave dangers or remarkable successes, to seek an interpretation beyond pure chance in their lives. In any case, I have personally experienced something in my life with all my being: whenever, for whatever reason, my head bows from the sky toward the earth, an unpredictable and entirely unplannable event lifts my head upward. I have such faith in this experience that even if, hypothetically, all sciences and philosophies were to conclude that there's nothing up there, it would have the slightest effect on my faith in this experience! Based on my inner and outer experiences, I have accepted that not only is there something up there, but everything ends and culminates there. Hence, the most delightful and sweetest moments of my life have always been when I hold my head high. It's clear that by "up" I don't mean the geographical sense of the word. Up exists in all dimensions of being and in all directions. This too is a way of living in an era that some have perhaps wrongly or exaggeratedly called the age of the eclipse of God!#Ahmad_Zeydabadi @ahmadzeidabad

Order to silence! The last time I told someone it would be better to stay silent instead of speaking was in the middle of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's first presidential term, addressing the late Seyed Ebrahim Nabavi. Of course, I didn't want him to be silent, but rather advised him to focus on satire and not get into serious political issues! entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] The Path of Return Iranians abroad who see things differently from what is…
entry.summary:

The Path of Return
Iranians abroad who see things differently from what is commonly called the "opposition" come under psychological and media pressure. Artists, in particular, are more exposed to such pressures and negative propaganda. Eventually, a time comes when they prefer returning to their homeland, despite all its problems, over enduring those conditions, and they set their sights on going back to their birthplace. With such a decision, the political atmosphere abroad intensifies against them, and they become the target of the darkest accusations. In fact, part of the opposition seeking the overthrow of the Islamic Republic, on the one hand, treats Iranian artists abroad with utter cruelty and intolerance at the slightest divergence from their own views, and on the other hand, blocks their path back to the homeland and out of that toxic environment with endless insults! Apparently, their goal is for these artists to remain in that foreign land and die of grief! Any artist or any intellectual who does not succumb to this atmosphere and chooses the path of return to their country should be congratulated and welcomed. Living in one's homeland is the natural and God-given right of every Iranian and has nothing to do with the government. Those who deny this right or tarnish its exercise are both cut from the same cloth, standing at the two extremes of the axis of villainy! #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

The work of Channel 3 or Netanyahu's design? Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, in reaction to reports about an assassination plot against Barron Trump, the 20-year-old son of the US president, has said: "The claim of a plot against Trump's son is nothing but a big lie that Netanyahu has designed to deceive and frighten the US president." The reality is that before Israeli officials raised this issue, Channel 3 of IRIB of the Islamic Republic aired a video titled "Where should we kill Barron Trump?" in which it reported the existence of a plot to assassinate Trump's son! In fact, Israeli circles, citing this very film, have claimed that the Islamic Republic has a plan to kill Trump's son! Given the denial by the secretary of the National Security Council of any plan by the Islamic Republic to assassinate Barron Trump and attributing the raising of this claim to Netanyahu, the question now arises: with what motive and on whose orders did Channel 3 of IRIB broadcast a film whose claim Mr. Rezaei has deemed to be Netanyahu's design, propaganda, and fabrication? #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] It needs no one's permission, but... Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the parliament…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

It needs no one's permission, but... Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the parliament speaker, has said: "The strategic relations between China and Iran need no one's permission." Yes, they need no one's permission, but do the Chinese really consider their relationship with Iran strategic? Mr. Ghalibaf has intended to travel to Beijing since his appointment as the Islamic Republic's special envoy for China affairs, but so far this trip has not materialized. Is this a coincidence? Or are the Chinese upset and angry over Iran's lack of negotiation with the US, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, threats to the energy resources of Arab Gulf states by some circles in Tehran, and especially the Houthis' actions against Saudi Arabia? China, which imports more than 40 percent of its consumed oil through the Strait of Hormuz, how could it possibly be pleased with the closure of the strait? The Saudi newspaper Arab News has reported on a high-level meeting between Chinese officials and members of the Gulf Cooperation Council in Riyadh in recent days. According to the report, "Senior officials praised the remarkable progress in implementing agreements between the parties since the announcement of the strategic partnership between the GCC and China in December 2022 and discussed initiatives to strengthen this cooperation." Doesn't this kind of news explain the direction of China's foreign policy in our region more clearly than Mr. Ghalibaf's remarks?#احمد_زیدآبادی@ahmadzeidabad
